summary: Paper W4361199658 proposes a Chiplet Multi-Objective Optimization (CMO) algorithm for 2.5-D heterogeneous IC thermal and communication-aware placement. The scenario involves a 12-chiplet Multi-Window Display (MWD) system with passive interposer integration, mesh NoC topology, and forced-convection fin-channel heatsink cooling. The paper reports peak temperature reduction from 381.41 K to 373.58 K (8.34 K improvement, though calculated difference is 7.83 K) and communication consumption reduction from 1026.72 µJ to 794.59 µJ via CMO algorithm with weight factor α=0.5. Hotspot 7.0 provides steady-state thermal analysis using fourth-order Runge-Kutta solver with compact RC circuit model. However, Studio simulation was not executed due to the feasibility verdict not_2d_applicable, which blocks all quantitative validation and direct numerical comparison.
limitations: Feasibility gate verdict not_2d_applicable prevents Studio 2D steady-state simulation; no independent thermal simulation baseline established for comparison

Evidence chain incomplete: all 79 evidence items lack valid PDF page pinning or asset locators, blocking deterministic claim validation; floorplan coordinates and power map provided in extraction but not independently cited against paper figures

Hotspot 7.0 configuration file (material properties, C4/microbump geometry, silicon interposer thickness, TIM properties) not supplied; compact thermal model assumptions (uniform power, uniform chiplet temperature) cannot be verified against true 3D heat spreading in passive interposer

Physical mismatches unresolved: (1) Manhattan distance metric in 2D mesh heuristic does not capture 3D TSV thermal coupling or actual interposer conduction pathways; (2) single convection coefficient applied despite fin-channel heatsink with stated 30 mm height and 1 mm fin width—non-uniform lateral airflow and local temperature variations not modeled; (3) chiplet spacing implementation unclear—blend stated as 2.5×2.5 mm actual vs 4.0×4.0 mm theoretical, but spacing value not explicit in thermal or power model

Workload and operating point frozen at constant power (325 W total) with static ambient 318.5 K; no transient profiles, no validation against measured silicon data, no comparison to other thermal simulators or single-objective benchmark [31] numerical results

Reported temperature improvement (8.34 K stated vs 7.83 K calculated from 381.41−373.58) exhibits minor discrepancy; communication savings (232.13 µJ) verified algebraically but no independent energy cost derivation provided for Ebit=0.186 parameter

CMO algorithm implemented in C++ but neither source code, executable, nor reproducible container released; paper states 'data reported in this study are included in the article' without linking external repository, archive, or supplementary material
